Romano: Cardinale remains ‘key player’ in Milan’s transfer business despite Krösche’s arrival

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (387 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Markus Krösche will soon get to work at AC Milan, but Gerry Cardinale will remain involved.
  • It has not been a very well-kept secret that Milan have been pushing for the arrival of Krösche since the summer, when it looked as though the German director was all set to arrive alongside Ruben Amorim, before Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Markus Krösche will soon get to work at AC Milan, but Gerry Cardinale will remain involved.

It has not been a very well-kept secret that Milan have been pushing for the arrival of Krösche since the summer, when it looked as though the German director was all set to arrive alongside Ruben Amorim, before Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that rather than turn to an alternative appointment, the Rossoneri decided to internally promote some figures while leaving the vacancy open. Ultimately they were waiting for developments on Krösche, and he officially left the Bundesliga side last month, leaving him available to finally join.

On Monday, there was talk of a release clause paid to Eintracht. In a video published on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano revealed some added information about Krösche’s imminent arrival and what it will mean regarding Cardinale’s involvement.

It has been revealed that “Confirmation has arrived, and I would say finally, also from Germany of something we have been telling you for weeks: Markus Krosche will be the newly introduced Head of Football at Milan. In Germany there has been a much slower narrative, much more, let’s say, Eintracht-centric,” he mentioned (via MilanNews).

“The reality is that Milan has had an agreement with Krosche for some time, Milan also has everything ready for the official announcement which is expected shortly. Milan will not pay 5 million, but 4 million euros in compensation to Eintracht Frankfurt to free Krosche, who already remarked goodbye to the German club some time ago.

It has been revealed that “He will be ready and operational from the beginning of December to work on the winter transfer market with Gerry Cardinale, Ruben Amorim and the entire work group that is dealing with Milan. So there were never any doubts whatsoever.

Sources indicate that “Markus Krosche is ready to take control of the Rossoneri mercato with Gerry Cardinale, who will be absolutely present, a key player, and involved. After Milan’s excellent victory against Frosinone, the Milan owner reiterated that if Milan competes for a player, it will be to win, not to participate. In short, this is another sign of Milan’s ambition.”.

Not a forward: Why Mikel Arteta may need to bolster surprise Arsenal position amid January twist

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (369 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11.
  • Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.
  • The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11.

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier right now providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Spurs finally score... but still lose

📅 16 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.
  • It could have been something different.
  • “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

Sources indicate that THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Industry observers note that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

It has been revealed that “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Industry observers note that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

According to recent reports, massive save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

Industry observers note that for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola mentioned. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Industry observers note that pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

It has been revealed that is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he demonstrated two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

It has been revealed that his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Sources indicate that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some crucial saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Industry observers note that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo remarked.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc.

🗣️ "The young players give us energy" 💪Andoni Iraola is very pleased with the way the Liverpool youngsters played after beating Spurs 3-1 at Anfield 👏#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup | @markpougatch | @Robbie9Fowler pic.twitter.com/bHjOrmccH2.

🗣️"Szoboszlai scores A LOT OF BANGERS"😂Needless to say Cody Gakpo was really impressed with Dominik Szoboszlai's goal for Liverpool 👏#ITVFootball | @LFC | @Carabao_Cup | @gabrielclarke05 pic.twitter.com/O3bs6Y9M2p.

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye.

"You can never take it for granted!"Cody Gakpo and Lewis Koumas on Liverpool's confident win over Spurs in the third round of the Carabao Cup 👏 pic.twitter.com/mGHo8FZGeE.

"I focus quite a lot on them, sometimes I get angry but it's part of me wanting them to succeed" 🔴"They deserve this, they know what the club means" Alexis Mac Allister was full of praise for Liverpool's youngsters after their 3-1 win over Spurs 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/RdEHZrv4Qy.

It has been revealed that “From Tottenham’s point of view, there were positives. They had a sharpness to their game. [Lucas] Bergvall did well. There is lots to look forward to for the weekend. It was a better performance. On another day, they could have had two or three goals. Liverpool just had enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that andrew Robertson received a great reception from the Anfield crowd whilst warming up, when he came on and now at full-time. He catches up with old teammates as he heads off in the pouring rain, applauding the Liverpool fans.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool book their place in the fourth round of the League Cup courtesy of a 3-1 win over Tottenham. Andoni Iraola’s side scored three stunning goals to seal their progression.

Mamardashvili does well to save from a deflection, like he did a few minutes ago. Mamardashvili did not cover himself in glory for Tottenham’s goal but has made some great saves tonight.

In a recent development, oh my word! The Hungarian loves a screamer and this is another to add to the list. It is similar to a goal Suarez scored at The Kop End against Norwich a number of years ago. Szoboszlai chests it down and from nearly 30 yards out smashes across the ball. The ball flies into to the top corner, always going away from Dubravka, and Szoboszlai celebrates in front of The Kop. A quite incredible goal.

It has been revealed that THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

There will be four added minutes at Anfield.

Savio has an effort from the right side of the box but drags his shot wide of the far post.

Liverpool counter with Mamardashvili’s long ball forward for Isak, who gets the better of Gray on the left side of the box. Isak gets his shot away and the ball appeared to hit Tosin’s arm but the penalty is not given. Replays show it did hit Tosin’s arm and he is lucky there is not VAR tonight as that could well have been overturned.

Sources indicate that solanke is on for Tottenham in place of Tel as the visitors have a corner out on the right. Tottenham take it short before the delivery is swung in and headed away by Gakpo as the rain comes thrashing down again at Anfield.

Industry observers note that tottenham keep it alive and Marmoush has an effort from the left side of the box. It deflects off Araujo and Mamardashvili makes a stunning save.

Szoboszlai should bury a guilt-edge chance inside the Tottenham penalty area but his effort is saved. There was a suspicion of offside against Szoboszlai but the flag did not go up. Szoboszlai was being played onside by quite some way by Gray so a huge missed opportunity.

In a recent development, that is superb one-vs-one defending from Jacquet. The ball is played down the left channel but Jacquet gets the better of Marmoush.

Into the final 10 minutes we go at Anfield.

Liverpool are under pressure at the moment as Tottenham attack the Anfield Road End, where the travelling Spurs supporters are housed. Mamardashvili is again unconvincing when dealing with a corner into the box.

Double change for Tottenham as Savio and Maddison replace Kudus and Gallagher.

Industry observers note that that is a stupid challenge from Kerkez, who is booked for a silly foul on Gallagher. Kerkez was asking for a booking for that challenge and referee Andy Madley obliges.

Change for Liverpool as Barcola replaces Ngumoha.

The visitors take advantage of very poor keeping from Mamardashvili. Fernandes’ delivery should be dealt with by Mamardashvili but the Georgian keeper flaps at empty air. It comes to Gallagher, who has a simple header from just a few yards out. A lifeline for Tottenham, who have their first goal this season against Premier League opposition.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

It has been revealed that tottenham have had some decent chances tonight. The latest comes for Gallagher just inside the Liverpool box but his effort takes a deflection off Kerkez and goes behind for a corner...

Sources indicate that that is a crucial challenge from Kerkez inside his own box. Marmoush looked like he was going to have a great opportunity from 10 yards out in the centre of Liverpool’s penalty area but Kerkez intervenes with a superbly-timed challenge to deny the Egyptian.

Double change for Liverpool as Szoboszlai and Gravenberch replace Nyoni and McConnell in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield.

Recent findings suggest that mamardashvili makes an important save. Marmoush carries the ball a long way down Tottenham’s left before cutting inside. As he gets to the Liverpool box, he plays the ball across to his right to find Kudus, whose first-time effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his left.

Robertson is going to come on for Tottenham against his former side and receives a great reception from the Liverpool fans, similarly to the reception Ray Clemence received all those years ago:.

Legendary goalkeeper, Ray Clemence would've turned 78 today ❤️Not many former players get a reception as good as this when they come back to Anfield, he was a true Liverpool great 🙌 pic.twitter.com/NLH3nZUJjd.

Fernandes is also on for the visitors.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Tosin decides to shoot from range but drags his effort wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

The home side double their lead at The Kop end. Kerkez perhaps should shoot from the edge of the box but instead lays it back to Mac Allister. The Argentine then plays it to his left to find Gakpo, who cuts inside onto his right and fires into the far corner. This now his tenth goal in 13 League Cup appearances.

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

No chances to speak of in the early stages of this second half.

It has been revealed that we are back under way at Anfield. Liverpool have made a change at the break with Jacquet coming on for Gomez. This was Gomez’s first game back after injury.

Tottenham did have two massive chances through Bergvall and Kudus and there are arguments to say both of them should have scored.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

We are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

This will be the final moment of the half.

Senesi absolutely clatters into McConnell but somehow escapes without a booking. There have been a number of soft yellows in this first yet one of the most blatant yellows is not given as a booking.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

That is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

According to recent reports, there is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

It has been revealed that that is a big chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

Recent findings suggest that what a goal......that would of been! 🫢Kudus fires over what would of been a sensational move from Spurs#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/a1TPzKyJlP.

Gomez gives the ball away cheaply inside his own half before McConnell is penalised for a foul on Marmoush. Will Tottenham cross it or take the shot on from around 25 yards out? The answer is the latter and Marmoush goes for goal but misses the target.

Sources indicate that that was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a fresh contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

According to recent reports, koumas comes close to putting Liverpool in front with their first real chance of the game. Ngumoha slides a clinical pass into the box to pick out the run in behind of Koumas, who gets the better of Senesi. Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

Close for Lewis Koumas!The Liverpool youngster is denied by Martin Dubravka after some brilliant play by Rio Ngumoha 🪄 pic.twitter.com/YNC8QEAGGG.

Recent findings suggest that given their team has been bang average this season, the huge number of travelling Spurs fans are making a magnificent noise. They could have celebrated a long-overdue goal had it not been for a magnificent save by Giorgi Mamardashvili. The Georgian needed to make it from Lucas Bergvall, as a minute beforehand he dithered while Joe Gomez was shepherding a ball back to him and those on the Kop lost their minds. It’s tense amongst Liverpool supporters. You wonder how it changes.

That is a fantastic save from Mamardashvili. Gallagher plays the ball to Udogie on the left side of the box and the latter squares it to Bergvall in the centre of the box. Bergvall is no more than eight yards out and must think he is going to score but Mamardashvili makes a great save to deny the Swede. Should Bergvall have given Mamardashvili the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Tottenham are dominating possession thus far, with a lot of the game being played in Liverpool’s half at the moment.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

In a recent development, tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Industry observers note that gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Sources indicate that tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Kudus keeps it alive and sends in another cross that ends up in Mamardashvili’s arms.

We are under way at Anfield, with a place in the fourth round at stake.

Industry observers note that A reminder, there is no extra time so it the game is all square after 90 minutes we will go straight to penalties. Also, there is no VAR tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. In Virgil van Dijk’s absence, Joe Gomez captains Liverpool tonight. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Araujo, Gomez, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Nyoni, McConnell, Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.Substitutes: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Szoboszlai, Isak, Munoz, Barcola, Gravenberch, Chambers.

Tottenham: Dubravka; Gray, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie; Bentancur, Bergvall; Kudus, Gallagher, Tel; Marmoush.Substitutes: Kinsky, Robertson, Van Hecke, Maddison, Savio, Fernandes, Solanke, Davies, Van de Ven.

"We have to be patient, I thought it was too much for him at Bournemouth at the start, but he got it right"Jamie Redknapp says Andoni Iraola "needs time" at Liverpool to implement his methods 💬 pic.twitter.com/hCVeZJ3qSn.

🗣️ If it was a school report it would be 'must do better'Robbie Fowler gives his views on Liverpools start to the season under Andoni Iraola 🔴#ITVFootball | @Robbie9Fowler | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/rgo68N07Fa.

🗣️ "It's a lot of changes" Andoni Iraola explains why he's made 🔟 changes to the Liverpool starting 11 to face Spurs at Anfield 👀⁰#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/W3zy9aPbz2.

Let's get to work 💪 pic.twitter.com/ji1hsS4tyt.

According to recent reports, andrew Robertson played nearly 400 games for Liverpool and won countless trophies with the club, including two Premier League titles, two League Cups and the Champions League. Upon his return to Anfield, he starts on the bench against his former employers.

Djaksparo is a rising musician from Paris who who gained viral fame following a social media boost from Liverpool’s summer signing Bradley Barcola, who is on the bench for the hosts this evening.

Welcome to Anfield, Djaksparo 👋 pic.twitter.com/iueYa1KjL7.

"I would like to see the goals!"Roberto De Zerbi ahead of Spurs clash with Liverpool in the Carabao Cup 🙌 pic.twitter.com/uSjCJcnAfJ.

Richarlison is not happy at Roberto de Zerbi's decision to leave him out of Tottenham's squad tonight 🙅‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/WqRWb3KPed.

Industry observers note that “There is no joy watching Spurs at the moment. Last year was a survival job, but now you have got to flip it. [Roberto] De Zerbi’s got a lot of players at his disposal.

In a recent development, “He has got to fit that jigsaw puzzle together. There are still a lot of elements that are not right; they have not got a left-sided player they can trust in. Goals have been a real problem, but I do think they will come.”.

During the Spaniard’s three seasons at the helm at Bournemouth, he never made it past the fourth round in this competition. He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Just one player remains from Liverpool’s starting XI against Fulham on Saturday and that is Ronald Araujo. Virgil van Dijk and Florian Wirtz are given the night off for the home side.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Araujo, Gomez, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Nyoni, McConnell, Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.Substitutes: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Szoboszlai, Isak, Munoz, Barcola, Gravenberch, Chambers.

Roberto De Zerbi makes eight changes from Tottenham’s draw against Everton, with Archie Gray, Rodrigo Bentancur and Omar Marmoush the three players to remain in the starting XI.

Tottenham: Dubravka; Gray, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie; Bentancur, Bergvall; Kudus, Gallagher, Tel; Marmoush.Substitutes: Kinsky, Robertson, Van Hecke, Maddison, Savio, Fernandes, Solanke, Davies, Van de Ven.

We're in the building 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/nPJefN5F3A.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Peterborough vs Barnsley 7.30pmWest Ham vs Fulham 7.45pmIpswich vs Arsenal 8pmLiverpool vs Tottenham 8pmReading vs Brentford 8pm.

Our Spurs side to take on Liverpool 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/X4f3F0cl4f.

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola noted. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no challenges. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

In a recent development, “I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I stated we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

West Ham team news and predicted XI to face Stoke City as Scott Parker bids to stop dismal form

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scott Parker’s return to West Ham has proved far from straightforward, with the former midfield cult hero yet to pick up his first three points in charge at WHUFC.

In a recent development, presently sitting 13th place and three points off the Championship play-off positions, a 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth exemplified their goal-scoring struggles of late. Despite leading the division for goals scored, the Hammers have repeatedly struggled to apply the clinical finishing touch in recent weeks.

In a recent development, registering an astonishing 144 shots across their last six games without securing a single victory, their attacking potency has faded. And, a clash with high-flying Stoke City isn’t exactly the game West Ham would want to arrest their recent struggles.

Mark Robins’ side arrive as the division’s form team, winning their last five on the spin to move into 2nd.

One positive for Parker is that he has a plethora of options to pick from on Saturday, with only a few injury concerns.

Alphonse Areola has been out since the defeat to Blackburn Rovers earlier this month due to a knock suffered in the warm-up. West Ham full-back Kyle Walker-Peters is also expected to be unavailable, with the defender still recovering from a muscle strain.

In a recent development, keiber Lamadrid has only played 21 minutes of Championship football this term due to a knee injury sustained in September. He will be absent against the Potters, with a return expected in the coming weeks.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek, Mukasa, Engels; Austbo, Bowen; Piroe.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeping department has been one of the biggest concerns for West Ham this term due to the poor performances of Mads Hermansen and the injury struggles of Areola. However, Finlay Herrick has played admirably since coming into the side against Preston and will likely be in between the sticks.

Fellow academy graduate Ezra Mayers has also received more minutes since Parker’s arrival and should be given the nod at left-back, with Joel Veltman on the right.

Boasting the highest goal tally of any defender in the division with six, Konstantinos Mavropanos has been a mainstay at centre-back with Max Kilman as his partner, although his recent shaky displays could mean Morato comes in.

Edson Alvarez returned after a three-month absence against Preston and revealed his worth at the base of West Ham’s midfield. However, having also played on Tuesday night, the Mexican’s minutes need to be managed, so Tomas Soucek could replace him.

Despite dividing opinion with his displays in the middle of the park, Arne Engels has performed well of late and will likely partner Divine Mukasa in a more advanced midfield role.

Arne Engels’ Championship stats.

Sources indicate that jarrod Bowen has been WHUFC’s go-to man this term, registering seven goals and seven assists, and the captain will be on the right. The opposite flank is up for grabs though, with the lively Edvin Austbo potentially getting selected ahead of the inconsistent Manor Solomon.

Striker is a problem area, but Joel Piroe will likely get the nod once again.

#165537. The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.
  • While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United plan to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, presently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Recent findings suggest that collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Industry observers note that mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

Industry observers note that in the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Industry observers note that richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and highlighted last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

Sources indicate that united have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

Recent findings suggest that one option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and indicated he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Sources indicate that milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

Industry observers note that united should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – important given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ remarked Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

According to recent reports, pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an glitch here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City will head into the month of December as automatic promotion contenders in the Championship, having finally found their spark under Chris Davies.

A 10th-placed finish in the second tier last year, just 12 months after their 111-point haul in League One, was respectable enough, but there was always the scope for more to come from Davies' squad, and they're really showing it now.

Whilst Blues look to have depth all over the pitch, one area that they could look to bolster in the upcoming January transfer window is at the top end.

He had a slow start to life in the Midlands since his £6 million move from Djurgardens in January, but August Priske has finally come alive in the Championship.

The 22-year-old Dane found the back of the net just once from his 17 Championship appearances in the second half of 2025-26, but now acclimatised to English football, he's scored seven goals in 13 outings so far in the current campaign.

Priske has forged a good understanding with Jay Stansfield in the number 10 role, but his understudies have made little impact, with German veteran Marvin Ducksch and summer recruit Luis Vazquez both failing to fire off the bench.

It leaves Davies with a dilemma ahead of January - do City let one of the pair go and bring in a new striker to battle with Priske in the second half of the season as they push for the Premier League?

Blues may do just that, as reports have been emerging about a potential striker transfer target that is based in Spain.

According to a report from Ficherío, Sevilla forward Isaac Romero is on the club's radar ahead of the window's opening at the start of 2027, with the 26-year-old Spaniard growing frustrated with life at Los Nervionenses due to a lack of game-time this season.

It's claimed that Birmingham are already in contact with the agents of Romero in regards to a deal, and that a 'significant salary' has been put on the table for him to make the move to the second tier of English football - albeit it's also reported that Romero would like to stay at Sevilla if he gets more chances of minutes.

Romero was plucked from lower league Spanish outfit Antoniano in 2019, having started his youth career with Sevilla, making his first-team debut in 2024 for the club.

Starting in just four of his 11 La Liga appearances, Romero is behind Lucas Stassin and Robbie Ure in the pecking order, but he's scored more goals than the pair put together so far in the Spanish top flight, netting three times compared to Stassin and Ure's two goals combined.

According to recent reports, if Birmingham make good progress with a move to sign Romero from Sevilla, then it could spark a departure from St. Andrew's - but not necessarily from their striker unit.

Reports from earlier in the week claim that Sevilla have an interest in signing Blues winger Carlos Vicente, who hasn't found his best form since signing from Alaves for £7 million last January.

Vicente worked under current Sevilla boss Luis Garcia Plaza whilst he was the manager of Alaves, and he's reportedly keen to re-unite with the 27-year-old just a year after he departed for England.

Industry observers note that would Isaac Romero be a good signing for Birmingham City? Comment below!

Pushed behind Patrick Roberts in the pecking order more often than not this season under Davies, Vicente could potentially play a part in a swap deal if all parties agree to it, but if initial reports are to be believed, it may be tough to get Romero out of Sevilla given he has a point to prove.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

  • Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.
  • Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:55.

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Blackpool form (all competitions):.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles.

With one of the best defensive sides in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we expect Boro to edge a low-scoring contest.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United laid down their promotion credentials in their midweek draw against Southampton, and now travel to the capital to take on another top eight side in QPR.

The Blades had gotten to the periphery of the play-offs on a rather favourable run of fixtures. With Southampton, QPR, West Brom and Middlesbrough to play between last Tuesday and Boxing Day, we were going to find out a lot about how serious this side is.

And while it may only be one game in that run of four against sides in the top eight, their performance for the final hour against the Saints was very impressive, and while their equaliser didn't come until the 90th minute, they were good value for that, and maybe even more.

Now they have to back that up and take on a QPR side who have been one of the more well-organised outfits in the division so far this season. The Hoops have the third-best overall xGA, the best from set pieces, and have faced the fourth-fewest shots.

Sheffield Wednesday have announced a major ticketing decision ahead of tomorrow afternoon's League One fixture against Reading at Hillsborugh.

Positioned fourth in League One at this moment in time, the Owls are striving to close the gap and edge closer to the automatic promotion places but are just five points ahead of tomorrow's opponents, who remain in ninth and have won only one of their last six outings across all competitions.

Attendances at Hillsborough have been strong since David Storch's much-welcomed takeover of the club at the end of the previous campaign, and with an average figure just shy of 31,000 across their eight home fixtures to date in league action, more of the same is in order for Reading's visit.

As confirmed via the club's social media channels on Friday afternoon, Wednesday will be opening their turnstiles to fans of the Sheffield-based non-league club, who have been competing in the Northern Premier League East this term.

The offer will only be applicable to season ticket holders at Sandygate, which just happens to be world football's oldest ground. Indeed, Hallam FC are the world's second-oldest club, too, though this announcement comes upon the seventh-tier outfit's confirmation that they would be withdrawing from the seventh-tier with immediate effect following a warning that they could run out of money as early as next month.

Facing the threat of extinction owing to a "perilous" financial situation, Wednesday have extended an invitation for free attendance to all Hallam FC season ticket holders, who are able to claim their complimentary ticket in the West Stand Lower on Leppings Lane by showing their season ticket at turnstiles 14 and 17.

The Owls have penned a warm-natured message of goodwill and support to their non-league neighbours, too, having travelled to Sandygate in pre-season, and the gesture has garnered quite the reaction online.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Sources indicate that but United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Industry observers note that however, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

Industry observers note that ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ mentioned Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a latest contact stalled.

Industry observers note that ‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Recent findings suggest that asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

AC Milan are not just looking for a newly introduced source of goals in January. They are also searching for ways to help create them and keep them out.

According to recent reports, as Calciomercato.com report, Gerry Cardinale is determined to refine Ruben Amorim’s squad, which needs more quality and depth. Endrick remains the headline name that Milan are pursuing, but the idea of signing a left-back is gaining momentum swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that while waiting for the arrival of Markus Krösche to be made official, work is already underway to examine the possibility of signing a new defender. The very likely departure of Pervis Estupinan – who has suitors in Spain – could help facilitate a winter swoop for a left-sided player.

Industry observers note that noussair Mazraoui is one option, whose contract with Manchester United expires in 2028. It’s too early to know whether he’ll be a valuable asset to upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino, but Amorim is an admirer of his and the Moroccan could be a versatile and experienced asset.

According to recent reports, another player whose contract expires in a year and a half is Alejandro Balde, whom Barcelona are looking to sell in January after unsuccessful attempts over the summer. His agent Jorge Mendes has offered him to several clubs, including Milan.

The directors are keeping him on their list. This year, he’s made just five appearances for a total of 125 minutes across LaLiga and the Champions League. So, he might have to leave the Blaugrana to play more regularly.

There are a couple of domestic options too. Gabriele Calvani is shining for Frosinone (though he struggled on Sunday in his San Siro audition). The 22-year-old centre-back can play full-back, and while he is owned by Genoa, the two clubs are in talks over Christian Comotto which could aid things.

Juan Miranda is the other name, even though he is negotiating a contract renewal with Bologna given his deal expires in 2028. The Spaniard is an old favourite having been linked before, and he would be expected to cost €15m or more.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.
  • Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.
  • Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Swindon Town are on the search for a newly introduced manager, with Ian Holloway's time at the County Ground coming to an end earlier in the week.

The 63-year-old had been in charge of the Robins for the past two years, having endured a storied career which has taken him to the Premier League with both Blackpool and Crystal Palace.

Improvement was highlighted in both seasons finished by Holloway, with 12th and ninth-placed finishes in League Two, but results have been indifferent during the current campaign, with back-to-back defeats over Grimsby Town and Newport County leading to his dismissal.

Swindon's hierarchy - which includes chairman Clem Morfuni - must now find Holloway's successor, and FLW can exclusively reveal that one individual who is on the radar is none other than Premier League legend Robbie Fowler.

Fowler scored 163 Premier League goals in his career for Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City, whilst also appearing 26 times for the England national team, before winding down his career in Australia and Thailand.

Since his retirement, Fowler has been well-travelled as a manager, with spells in both Thailand and Australia, as well as India and Saudi Arabia, but he's yet to land a job in his native England, having been without a role since being with Al-Qadsiah in 2023.

That could now change though, with Football League World understanding that the 51-year-old is a live contender to become the latest person to have a go at the Town job.

One of the reasons that Fowler is being admired by Swindon chairman Morfuni is his time in his native Australia, FLW can reveal.

After a spell at Blackburn Rovers, Fowler moved down under in 2009 to play for North Queensland Fury, a stint which lasted a year before moving on to fellow Aussie club Perth Glory.

Fowler would join Muangthong United in Thailand in 2011 and end up becoming their player-manager for a short period of time, but some eight years after leaving Australia, the former striker would return as a manager, taking the Brisbane Roar job.

Managing 23 games for the Queensland-based outfit, Fowler won 11 times as their manager, before the A-League was suspended in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic - he wouldn't return to the club as he relocated to be closer to his family.

A further 20 matches were managed for East Bengal between 2020 and 2021, before a stint in Saudi with Al-Qadsiah lasted just three months, despite winning six of his eight matches in charge and going unbeaten in the Saudi second tier, with the club wanting to move to a more Spanish-style model, according to Fowler himself.

Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s new biology skills wow scientists
