Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

In a recent development, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

According to recent reports, the Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Industry observers note that much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

According to recent reports, the Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Industry observers note that bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

Industry observers note that the midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

Industry observers note that his absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

It has been revealed that chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a latest contract.

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Two teams at the bottom of the Scottish Premiership standings will do battle on Saturday, when St Mirren welcome Kilmarnock to the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

The hosts are 10th in the table with 14 points from 14 games, while the visitors are propping up the standings with just nine points from 14 fixtures.

St Mirren initially enjoyed a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning three and drawing one of their opening four league fixtures.

However, Craig McLeish's side subsequently endured a miserable run of results, going on to record just one win in their next 10 league fixtures.

The Saints have suffered eight defeats during that run, alongside one draw, leading to St Mirren rapidly falling to 10th in the Scottish Premiership table with just 14 points.

St Mirren, now just one point above the drop zone, face a particularly key match in the early relegation battle, as a win against Kilmarnock would extend their lead over the bottom-placed side to a healthy eight points.

On the other hand, a defeat, which would mark their fourth consecutive loss, would see St Mirren's current five-point lead slashed to just two points.

Despite their ongoing struggles, the Saints have been at their best at home, including winning one, drawing one and losing one of their last three home fixtures.

Kilmarnock, meanwhile, are enduring a dismal 2026-27 league campaign, sitting at the bottom of the standings with just nine points after 14 matchdays.

Neil McCann's side have recorded two wins, three draws and suffered nine defeats in their 14 league games, including remaining winless in their last five matches, with four losses and one draw.

Kilmarnock's biggest weakness has undeniably been their defensive vulnerability, having conceded 33 goals in 14 league matches - seven more than any other team in the division.

However, Killie are equally ineffective in offence, having scored just 15 goals in 14 games - only St Mirren (13) have scored fewer in the league.

Despite their disappointing campaign to date, Kilmarnock do boast a strong recent record against St Mirren, winning three of the last five encounters, although they did lose 1-0 earlier this term.

Kilmarnock Scottish Premiership form:.

St Mirren will be without Nikolas Agrafiotis, Jonah Ayunga, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus for this match due to injury problems.

Killian Phillips is St Mirren's top scorer (four) and joint-top assister (two) in the league this season, and the attacking midfielder should start behind Eseosa Sule in attack.

Meanwhile, Max Stryjek remains unavailable due to a knee injury, leaving Nico Mantl to continue in goal.

George Stanger and Michael John Kamara should provide protection in central defence, with Tom Lowery, Aaron Tshibola and Greg Kiltie featuring in midfield.

St Mirren possible starting lineup:.

Chapman; Ramsay, Gogic, Jackson, John; Carr, Nsio; Thomas, Phillips, Kabia; Sule.

Kilmarnock possible starting lineup:.

Mantl; McCarthy, Kamara, Stanger, Schjonning-Larsen; Tshibola, Lowery; Ring, Kiltie, Owen; Hugill.

St Mirren may be enduring a run of three straight defeats, but the hosts have been at their best at home and they remain the favourites to take all three points from the struggling Kilmarnock.

In a recent development, arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

According to recent reports, as the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

According to recent reports, arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

According to recent reports, the visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

Sources indicate that but Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

Industry observers note that london City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

In a recent development, delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some upcoming energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

According to recent reports, the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

According to recent reports, on his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. According to recent reports, “As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

It has been revealed that “When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”.

In a recent development, “I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”.

Recent findings suggest that “In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. Now down to third in the Serie A standings, Scudetto holders Inter Milan will try to give their title defence a boost when Genoa visit San Siro on Saturday night.

Recent results have seen Inter slip behind both Rome clubs, but they gained a vital European victory in midweek; meanwhile, their visitors have surged into the top half after recovering from a rocky start.

Having exited at the first knockout round last season, Inter started this term's Champions League campaign by taking nothing from their first two fixtures - but​ things have improved dramatically since then.

Three straight wins without conceding have moved them up the table, and Cristian Chivu's side now occupy a playoff place - in fact, finishing inside the top eight cannot be ruled out.

After defeating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord, the Nerazzurri beat Stuttgart 2-0 on Wednesday night, as captain Lautaro Martinez scored his first goal since returning from injury.

That partly made amends for throwing away two Serie A points three days beforehand, when Inter played out a chaotic 4-4 draw with local rivals Atalanta BC.

Despite Pio Esposito's first top-flight hat-trick, they let in a couple of avoidable late goals that left them three points behind surprise leaders Lazio, with Roma sandwiched between.

Now, the Nerazzurri will aim to put pressure on both capital clubs by posting a customary home win over Genoa.

Such has been their dominance, Inter have won all of the last 12 league meetings at San Siro, keeping 10 clean sheets and only conceding two goals.

Either home or away, Genoa have won none of their last 14 clashes with Inter, so they may be dreading an upcoming double-header.

Just days after this league game, the Grifone must return to Milan for a cup tie, as the sides vie for a place in the Coppa Italia quarter-finals.

Though their past record makes for grim reading, present form suggests Genoa can at least give the Italian champions a scare, as they have won five of their last seven Serie A matches.

Since Daniele De Rossi swerved the sack during the October international break, his rejuvenated side have shot up the table, swapping the drop zone for the top half.

Last weekend, the Rossoblu beat lowly Sassuolo 2-0 thanks to a Milutin Osmajic brace, posting back-to-back away wins for the first time since 2024.

Some 12 years have passed since Genoa recorded three successive away wins at Italy's elite level, and few would expect them to do so on Saturday.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Inter will be missing set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu and back-up striker Ange Bonny due to thigh injuries, while Piotr Zielinski and Alessandro Bastoni are both doubts.

Bastoni was substituted before half time against Stuttgart, and it remains to be seen if he will recover from a muscular problem in time to play.

After scoring as a substitute in midweek, Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and in-form Esposito to feature up front.

Sources indicate that level with the latter pair in the Capocannoniere race, Genoa striker Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances. The Montenegrin is almost certain to start, as fellow forward Lorenzo Colombo suffered an ACL injury last weekend, probably curtailing his 2026-27 campaign.

Leo Ostigard was recently hospitalised with a high fever, but he is still expected to lead the visitors' three-man defence in Milan.

Key midfielder Morten Frendrup has been struggling with an ankle issue, meaning he faces a race against time.

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Saturday afternoon when they welcome Athletic Bilbao to Estadio La Rosaleda.

Athletic have won two of the last three meetings between the two sides and also lead the overall head-to-head record 13 victories to Malaga's 11.

Malaga held Athletic to a 3-3 draw when the pair last locked horns at La Rosaleda, while their last win over the Basque side was a 2-1 success in October 2016.

As for Athletic, a record of four wins, four draws and four defeats from 12 matches has left them eighth in the table on 16 points, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla heading into the next gameweek.

The Lions will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 defeat to Espanyol, which proved to be their first loss since October 21 away to Levante.

Edin Terzic's side have picked up 11 points from their seven home league matches this season, while they have claimed five points from their five games on their travels.

Athletic finished 12th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement during the current campaign, with a European spot certainly the target.

The Lions will take on Numancia in the Copa del Rey in their first match of December before hosting Real Madrid in their next league game on December 6.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in nine appearances for Malaga this season, and the 22-year-old is set to continue in the final third of the field.

As for Athletic, Unai Eguiluz, Gorka Guruzeta, Maroan Sannadi and Dani Vivian will miss the match due to injury problems.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.
  • Recent findings suggest that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Recent findings suggest that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

In a recent development, he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

According to recent reports, storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

In a recent development, storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Industry observers note that storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Sources indicate that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

According to recent reports, he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been hit by yet another injury ahead of facing Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier League.

The Seagulls were in action on Thursday night before lining up against Newcastle United.

The south coast club playing Universitatea Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Fabian Hurzeler needs as many players available as possible as he looks to compete in both Europe and the domestic competitions.

In the 39th minute of last night’s match, the Brighton boss saw Matt O’Riley on the end of a really poor challenge from Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu, who was then sent off after VAR review.

O’Riley tried to carry on but had to be replaced at the break and Fabian Hurzeler admitted after the match that it doesn’t look good for the Denmark international. The Brighton Head Coach revealing that the player’s ankle was very swollen.

This looks set to make it at least seven Brighton players ruled out of the Newcastle United match.

Malik Yalcouye was the latest long-term injury to hit the Seagulls ahead of last night’s game, whilst also ruled out are Kaoru Mitoma (knee), Stefanos Tzimas (thigh), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh).

Making it at least now seven Brighton players set to miss the Newcastle United match, as Joao Costinha is suspended after having been sent off during the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last weekend.

Other than the new injury for Fabian Hurzeler to deal with though, there wasn’t a lot of encouragement for Newcastle United from Brighton having this extra fixture to deal with ahead of Sunday.

The weak Conference League is very different to the demands of the Champions League.

Fabian Hurzeler was able to make eight changes and the Seagulls still cruised to victory against this weak Romanian opposition.

Only Maxim De Cuyper, Pascal Gross and Chema Andres stayed in the team from their Premier League defeat against Hull City and once they took the lead inside three minutes the result was never in doubt.

It has been revealed that they were two up after 33 minutes and then when the opposition went down to ten men it was easy street for the Brighton players. The final score ended up 4-0 but if they had really needed a bigger scoreline, who knows what it could have been if they had went all out in this game, rather than having both eyes on Newcastle United less than 72 hours later.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.
  • With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026.

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE.

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven.

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley.

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net.

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and notable for the win as well.'.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'.

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a fresh Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

Sources indicate that 1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week.

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week.

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week.

Recent findings suggest that 4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week.

Sources indicate that 5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week.

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Sources indicate that looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that he even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”.

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”.

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

Industry observers note that “We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

In a recent development, “And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

Industry observers note that “In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen fresh players.

Sources indicate that “We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been unveiled, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

Recent findings suggest that “Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I turned on the TV on Thursday night and I was puzzled, why were thousands of Sunderland fans banned from their latest European match?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I turned on the TV on Thursday night and I was puzzled, why were thousands of Sunderland fans banned from their latest European match?

The Mackems playing at the Stadium of Light in the Europa League.

Only the fifth European home match in the club’s entire history and yet Sunderland fans conspicuous by their absence.

The moment I switched on, the camera was focused on loads of sections of the Stadium of Light that were totally empty, no Sunderland fans in them at all.

I thought maybe I hadn’t heard of some UEFA ban that had forced them to close large parts of their stadium.

However, when the camera then focused elsewhere, there were many many empty seats in the areas of the ground that were open.

The match was woeful, the quality shocking, the only excitement when the cameras went back to the stands.

Recent findings suggest that it turns out the embarrassing number of empty seats would have been far worse but for loads of Jagiellonia Bialystok fans buying tickets amongst the Sunderland fans. Turns out the Polish team had seen their supporters banned from attending this match due to past misbehaviour.

This type of thing rarely ends well when you have a set of away fans banned and a home club that struggles to sell their tickets. Sure enough, the Police seemed to be having to wade into any number of sections to deal with friction between the Sunderland fans and the visiting supporters amongst them.

Away fans in the home end #SAFC https://t.co/CuaC6FUyVE.

— Sunderland Limbs 𝕏 (@LimbsSunderland) November 26, 2026.

Sources indicate that the actual match ended in a 1-1 draw and from what I saw, Sunderland very lucky to get a point against Jagiellonia Bialystok. Amusing to hear the booing from the few Sunderland fans who were still there at the final whistle.

The excitement of playing in Europe for only the second time in the club’s entire history, 53 years since the only other time, is now well and truly wearig off.

Polish club Jagiellonia Białystok were not supposed to have any away fans at The Stadium of Light for their game at Sunderland tonight due to a UEFA Disciplinary ruling, but loads of them are in the home end… 🫣😭 https://t.co/hBU0w02hYb.

— Football Away Days (@FBAwayDays) November 26, 2026.

In a recent development, I just checked the crowds and whilst the Mackems got 46,861 for their Premier League match against Arsenal, their Europa League home games have gone 45,555 against AZ Alkmaar, 44,269 v Dinamo Zagreb, last night 37,658. Sunderland fans deserting their team and the club having to totally close large areas of the Stadium of Light.

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most crucial positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the massive difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, introduced a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Industry observers note that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

It has been revealed that asked if Tottenham had made a substantial mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

In a recent development, that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Industry observers note that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

It has been revealed that jackson was not the only Villa latest boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery mentioned. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side at the moment sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Industry observers note that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

In a recent development, but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Christos Tzolis challenges Arsenal critics with a message about his physicality

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.
  • According to recent reports, since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium.
  • Industry observers note that but doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

According to recent reports, since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

Industry observers note that but doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he demonstrated little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Industry observers note that since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

He claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

This is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

Recent findings suggest that the Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

Sources indicate that in the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:58, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:04.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suarez has confirmed he is in talks with the MLS club over a fresh contract.

Suarez is in the closing stages of his third full season with Inter Miami after signing on a free transfer at the start of 2024.

The Uruguayan has scored 59 goals in 120 competitive appearances, including 17 strikes in 30 regular-season MLS games this season.

However, as it stands, Suarez is on course to become a free agent when his current deal expires at the end of the calendar year.

In theory, Friday's must-win playoff game against Columbus Crew could be his last, although he has revealed he is in talks over a fresh deal.

"We're already in talks with the club to find the best solution for both sides," Suarez told reporters on Wednesday.

"But honestly, my focus is more on the match against Columbus this Friday than on what will happen in the future.".

Inter Miami are one down in their three-match series against Columbus after falling to a heavy 3-0 defeat at the Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Gonzalo Tapia opened the scoring with a ninth-minute penalty, before Gonzalo Lujan's 36th-minute red card forced Inter Miami to play over 50 minutes with 10 men.

Columbus took full advantage to net two second-half goals to leave Inter Miami requiring a win at the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field to force a deciding game in the first-round tie.

Suarez has made it clear that "the time for excuses is over" as the Herons look to prolong their defence of the MLS Cup.

“It’s clear we are at a club where we have an obligation to win,” Suarez mentioned.

It has been revealed that “If we get eliminated on Friday, it will be a disappointment. We have to be that clear about it.

"The time for excuses is over...it’s time to face reality. If we are eliminated, we will be the first to be self-critical, although we hope that doesn’t happen.

“I believe the squad are at a point where we understand that it’s time to deliver. This is our final opportunity.

"This format has given us another chance to play this Friday, and it’s the last shot we have to bring the series back home.”.

The visitors experienced disappointment in their last trip to Columbus in September, when they fell to a 2-1 defeat following a stoppage-time winner.

The German international striker had a rollercoaster first season at Newcastle United, starting off in great form and then a bit like the team overall, found things more difficult as the 2025-26 campaign progressed and a 58 game season was far too much for a small squad to deal with.

A lot of nonsense written and spoken about Nick Woltemade with ridiculous claims he had been a total flop, despite having 14 direct goal involvements including scoring 11.

The decision was made for Nick Woltemade to spend the 2026-27 season with Juventus, Matthias Jaissle wanting to have pace as his main focus up front.

In a recent development, the hope being that a year of regular football in Italy will help Nick Woltemade improve his skill set, become better at holding the ball up, polish his goalscoring technique and so on. Helping him then to come back and be a bigger asset for the Newcastle United team, or command a significant transfer fee boosted by his time with Juventus.

Big Nick has had mixed fortunes with Juventus, not getting the amount of game time he would like (seven starts in all competitions, eight sub appearances) but doing very decently in the time he has spent on the pitch (five goals and three assists so far).

Industry observers note that last weekend with Juventus drawing 0-0 at home and booed off at half-time, Nick Woltemade was introduced for the second half and within 14 minutes had turned the game around, scoring one and then getting an assist. Juventus finally winning 4-0 at the end against Venezia and the United loan star picking up the MOTM award.

It was bench duties again last night, Nick Woltemade coming on in the second half with Juventus leading 3-1 against Omonia Nicosia in the second half and the Newcastle United loan striker helping his side to an eventual 4-1 victory.

A lot of daft transfer claims floating about and now the United striker’s agent has shot down one of the daftest.

Al-Maidan contacted Danny Bachmann, Nick Woltemade’s agent, to ask about media claims of Newcastle United doing a January 2027 swap deal, with 30-year-old Ivan Toney (reported to be on £20million a year/£400k a week, plus Toney has a court date to face in London after having been arrested and charged with an alleged serious assault in a nightclub) to come to United from Al Ahli and 24-year-old Nick Woltemade to join the Saudi club.

Danny Bachmann dismissing this speculation as laughable nonsense: “These reports are completely untrue.”.

In a recent development, the player’s agent making clear what the obvious reality is: “The player’s future will be decided at the end of the season when he returns to Newcastle United. We don’t know yet whether he will stay or leave.”.

How England could line up without Harry Kane as Thomas Tuchel given unusual solution (exclusive)

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:00.
  • England manager Thomas Tuchel has been told to consider an unusual solution to Harry Kane's injury absence if the Three Lions captain misses March's Nations League quarter-final with Norway.
  • Tuchel and co are sweating over the fitness of the Ballon d'Or winner after he was ruled out for a 'few months' with a serious ankle injury, sustained in Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:00.

England manager Thomas Tuchel has been told to consider an unusual solution to Harry Kane's injury absence if the Three Lions captain misses March's Nations League quarter-final with Norway.

Tuchel and co are sweating over the fitness of the Ballon d'Or winner after he was ruled out for a 'few months' with a serious ankle injury, sustained in Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln earlier this month.

Kane had to undergo surgery to correct the torn ligament, and there is a chance that he could now sit out the reunion with World Cup quarter-final foes Norway, whom the Three Lions face at the end of March 2027.

Tuchel has a plethora of alternative centre-forward options at his disposal, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Dominic Solanke, Ivan Toney, Ollie Watkins and Championship star Will Lankshear.

However, ex-England forward Brian Deane has exclusively told Sports Mole that Tuchel could instead consider using either Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers as a false nine rather than deploying a pure centre-forward.

“It is difficult because I do not think England have another centre-forward who can do exactly what Harry Kane does," Deane said. "He is not the quickest, but he is intelligent, drops into pockets and allows the team to rotate around him. He has earned the right for the manager to build that structure.

According to recent reports, “Dominic Calvert-Lewin is very good at holding the ball up, bringing others into play and competing in the air. Whether he would score the same types of goals as Kane is another question.

Recent findings suggest that “Solanke has the ability, but I am not convinced about his confidence at the moment. The England shirt can weigh heavily.

According to recent reports, “Ivan Toney has a strong all-round game, is excellent in the box and is one of the best penalty-takers around. The question would be how he adjusts to the tempo of international football from the league he is playing in.

“Will Lankshear is perhaps a little inexperienced. Bringing him into the squad is one thing; asking him to lead the line ahead of those other players is another.

“Tuchel might decide not to use a conventional centre-forward. He could put Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers further forward and approach it differently. It is very difficult to replicate Kane. He has done amazingly well and is almost irreplaceable.”.

According to data from Transfermarkt, Bellingham has only made one club appearance as an out-and-out centre-forward, compared to 23 for Rogers during his career.

If Deane's prediction comes true and Tuchel does opt for a false-nine approach, the Chelsea man should therefore be at the head of the queue for striking duties, especially having also featured in that role for the Blues already this season against Tottenham Hotspur.

Bellingham has licence to continue in the number 10 role as a result, and Rogers being moved centrally opens the door for a fit-again Bukayo Saka to reclaim his place on the right flank.

However, there is every chance that Kane will recover in time to face Norway, aiming to build on an unparalleled record of 93 goals in 127 matches for his country.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

It has been revealed that although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

In a recent development, bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an crucial role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Recent findings suggest that zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

In a recent development, newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

According to recent reports, konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

In a recent development, saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Industry observers note that newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors promptly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Sources indicate that overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

According to recent reports, it was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Recent findings suggest that milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

According to recent reports, frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

Sources indicate that however, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Industry observers note that frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Sources indicate that out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

According to recent reports, milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

According to recent reports, frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

In a recent development, the second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Industry observers note that ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

In a recent development, frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine quickly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Recent findings suggest that ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

Industry observers note that after the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

Industry observers note that for Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

With this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five significant chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction, Odds, H2H and Betting Tips

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The leaders of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga, under the lights at the Emirates.
  • David Raya is out, so Kepa gets the gloves, and Saturday’s 2-2 at St James’ Park showed that this team can still be got at.
  • The bookies make Arsenal strong favourites, as you’d expect with this home record in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The leaders of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga, under the lights at the Emirates. That’s the kind of Champions League night we waited years for, and now it’s a regular Tuesday. The champions are six points clear at home, unbeaten in Europe and up against a Dortmund side that hasn’t lost a league game all season.

There’s a twist, though. David Raya is out, so Kepa gets the gloves, and Saturday’s 2-2 at St James’ Park showed that this team can still be got at. This Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund preview covers everything you need before the 8pm kick-off. That means the latest odds, team news for both sides, predicted line-ups, the head-to-head record, the key stats and our prediction and betting tips.

The bookies make Arsenal strong favourites, as you’d expect with this home record in Europe. Dortmund are big outsiders for a side that’s top of the Bundesliga, and that tells you how highly the market rates the Gunners at the Emirates. Prices were checked on matchday and will move once the team sheets are out, so always check before you bet.

Those prices make Arsenal roughly a 67% chance, with the draw around 19% and Dortmund around 14% once the bookmaker margin is stripped out.

Be careful with the scorer lists, because some bookmakers still have Martin Zubimendi priced up and he’s injured.

Sources indicate that the significant news is in goal. Raya came off with a shoulder problem at Newcastle and Arteta confirmed he won’t be fit for tonight, though he noted it “doesn’t look too serious” and surgery isn’t needed. Kepa Arrizabalaga steps in.

According to recent reports, missing Saka is a blow, but Madueke has stepped up brilliantly. He rescued a point at Newcastle and Arteta called him “decisive” in his press conference. Zubimendi’s absence means Myles Lewis-Skelly is the most likely option to partner Declan Rice in midfield.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapié; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.

Saliba being back is a substantial boost, and there’s a real chance he comes straight in. Havertz is also pushing for a start up front.

Dortmund had two massive worries going into this one, and both look like they’ve cleared. Kovač said Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka trained on Monday and are “ready for tomorrow’s match”. Guirassy missed the weekend win at Gladbach with a hamstring problem, so whether he’s fit enough to start is still a question.

The exciting teenage midfielder swapping the Foxes for the Magpies.

(ED: Players generally cannot sign a professional contract until their 17th birthday. Under The FA’s Rule C11, players must be 18 or over to enter a playing contract unless they are 17 and not in full-time education.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

Recent findings suggest that despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

In a recent development, despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and rapidly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Industry observers note that just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

It has been revealed that A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

Despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Industry observers note that dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

It has been revealed that arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player rapidly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

It has been revealed that continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

According to recent reports, despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

Although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.
