📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

Sources indicate that but so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

In a recent development, it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

It has been revealed that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

In a recent development, it is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

In a recent development, it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

In a recent development, fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their upcoming head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

According to recent reports, but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Recent findings suggest that might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

Industry observers note that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

It has been revealed that michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

In a recent development, I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

According to recent reports, I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

Industry observers note that I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so key for us.

It has been revealed that there were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Industry observers note that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

In a recent development, I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

In a recent development, it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

Sources indicate that the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm.

According to recent reports, fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

United break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

Industry observers note that united may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

According to recent reports, manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

In a recent development, bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Industry observers note that fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

You would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

Recent findings suggest that here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

In a recent development, positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Sources indicate that fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Industry observers note that kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

According to recent reports, what a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”.

Sources indicate that well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

Recent findings suggest that "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

It has been revealed that fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

Fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the latest season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

In a recent development, more from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”.

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

It has been revealed that sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

In a recent development, nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

According to recent reports, united’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Sources indicate that josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

Industry observers note that this stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Sources indicate that bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

According to recent reports, fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Recent findings suggest that fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

In a recent development, A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Recent findings suggest that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Recent findings suggest that very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

In a recent development, if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Sources indicate that michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Industry observers note that subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

According to recent reports, the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick states Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a major impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager stated.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty significant one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he stated it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and upcoming head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

According to recent reports, fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are among Premier League clubs keeping a close eye on young defensive talent Joane Gadou, reports Mark Brus.

The Borussia Dortmund centre-back (19) signed for the Bundesliga giants this summer and has featured 17 times for them since (across all competitions).

Reporting for CaughtOffside’s The Daily Briefing, Mark Brus said: “I’m reliably told by sources with ties to the agents industry that Arsenal and other Premier League clubs have been closely monitoring Gadou for some time. The Frenchman only joined Dortmund this summer after impressing at Red Bull Salzburg, and he also had a spell in PSG’s academy earlier in his career.”.

According to recent reports, he went on to add that a source mentioned: “Arsenal got a close look at him yesterday, but the reality is that they have been monitoring Gadou for months. A lot of the top clubs know about him, even if they weren’t ready to move for him yet. I see him developing at Dortmund for a bit longer, but it’s clear how talented he is and if he carries on like this they won’t hold on to him for long.”.

Liverpool, Manchester United and Real Madrid are ‘keen’ on Gadou, but may have to come up against competition from PSG if the player continues his current developmental trajectory.

And that should come as no surprise to onlookers when the Frenchman is putting in top-quality displays of the calibre he produced against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

* Joane Gadou’s stats as per FotMob.

Combative, solid in the air, and against Mikel Arteta’s tricky Premier League champions. Notably, this hardly seems a fluke either, judging by the kind of numbers Joane Gadou is putting up for Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

* Joane Gadou’s stats in the 2026/27 Bundesliga season (via FotMob).

Between Giovanni Leoni, Jeremy Jacquet, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, high-potential, young centre-backs are hardly in short supply at L4.

That’s not to say there’s never any justification for adding more talent to the club ranks, but the problem Liverpool are facing at the end of the 2026/27 season dictates that the club should be looking at experienced operators.

As things currently stand, Virgil van Dijk has no clear idea whether he’s staying or going in the summer, and there’s yet to be any kind of guarantee around Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo.

We strongly suspect that Liverpool will have serious conversations about the Dutchman and his Uruguayan teammate given the pair’s strong performances this term. However, there remains a possibility that the Reds could be left incredibly short on experienced heads by the summer transfer window.

If that’s the case, this should be an absolute priority at the back over landing someone of Gadou’s profile.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 16:40, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:42.

An important game at the bottom end of the League One table will take place at the Cherry Red Records Stadium on Saturday, as AFC Wimbledon welcome Barnsley.

The hosts sit 18th but only lead the drop zone by three points while their visitors are rooted to the foot of the division and in the midst of a losing run.

AFC Wimbledon are back in League One action on Saturday in search of a second straight home victory to extend their lead over the relegation zone.

The Dons enjoyed a positive start to their second straight campaign in the third tier, earning 12 points from their first eight outings, but they were quickly dragged towards the bottom end of the division, losing four and drawing one of the next five matches.

They scored just three goals in those matches and at the moment have a league-low tally of 11 goals from 18 games, albeit they were able to make a crucial return to winning ways at home to Blackpool in mid-November, as Alistair Smith's early goal made the only difference.

Johnnie Jackson's men were unable to build on that last time out, though, visiting Leyton Orient and losing 4-1 having trailed by three at the break and pulled one back through Harry Cornick only for Alex Gilbert to put the game out of sight 20 minutes from time.

Now sat 18th, just three points and two places above the bottom four, and with just one league win on the board since mid-September, AFC Wimbledon will again bid to bounce back on Saturday and move further clear of the drop zone and towards mid-table.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head south aiming to arrest a bigger slump which has seen them cut adrift at the bottom of the table.

Daniel Stendel's return to the Barnsley dugout for the 2026-27 season has not gone to blueprint thus far, as the Yorkshire outfit sit bottom of League One on just nine points from 15 games having won just two and lost 10 of those.

One of those wins and six defeats have come from the Reds' eight away league games thus far, conceding 16 goals in those, while Stendel's men are winless in 11 third-tier outings since early September including three straight defeats heading into the weekend and seven in their last eight.

Following 2-1 losses to Wigan Athletic and South Yorkshire rivals Sheffield Wednesday, they visited Bradford City on Tuesday and suffered a 3-0 beating as Stephen Humphrys scored a brace and Jake Beesley added a late third.

Now rooted to the bottom of the league, four points behind the four teams above them, Barnsley will be desperate to end their long wait for a victory on Saturday and begin climbing towards safety after their dismal start.

AFC Wimbledon form (all competitions):.

Barnsley form (all competitions):.

AFC Wimbledon remain without forward Mathew Stevens due to a long-term injury, while Dujuan Richards and Dan Sweeney are also sidelined.

Attacker Jayden Stockley is back in contention, though, after a suspension last time out, and he will return up front having scored six of the Dons' 11 league goals so far this season.

Cornick will hope to join him, having scored in Stockley's absence at the weekend, with Miles Hippolyte also hoping to continue in an attacking role.

Barnsley are unable to call on attackers Amani Richards, Fabio Jalo and Tobi Adeyemo on Saturday.

Stendel may make changes from the midweek 3-0 loss, with Jubril Okedina in line to return to the defence and Daniel Johnson an option to join Luca Connell in midfield.

That would allow top scorer and captain Cameron McGeehan to return to an advanced midfield role, where he, Reyes Cleary and Vimal Yoganathan may support a lone striker.

AFC Wimbledon possible starting lineup:.

Bishop; Sessegnon, Ogundere, Johnson, Seddon; Nelson, Maycock, Browne; Cornick, Stockley, Hippolyte.

Barnsley possible starting lineup:.

Slicker; Okedina, Kay, Gale, Larkeche; Johnson, Connell; Yoganathan, McGeehan, Cleary; Kirk.

Both teams will see Saturday's game as a big opportunity to begin turning their form around and it could be a crucial one between the division's worst attack and its second-worst defence and most out-of-form team.

Barnsley look totally devoid of confidence, though, while AFC Wimbledon were able to get the better of Blackpool when they last met fellow strugglers, making them favourites with the best football betting sites, and we give an edge to the hosts as a result.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Sources indicate that speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

According to recent reports, “[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

Recent findings suggest that “[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”.

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

Industry observers note that exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Recent findings suggest that austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

Chelsea are reportedly interested in bringing Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger back to Stamford Bridge during the January transfer window.

Xabi Alonso's men are in need of fresh options at the back following last weekend's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds United, with the backline of the hosts capitulating against Daniel Farke's European hopefuls.

Looking to make swift amends, Chelsea travel to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest in the Premier League on Friday night, when the Blues will fight to record their first win since returning from the November international break.

Yet to reach his potential since joining the West Londoners, centre-back Wesley Fofana has faced criticism from his own boss following comments during an interview which put the Chelsea defender's commitment to the project in doubt.

Across Premier League and EFL Cup action, the Blues have won just one of their past five matches, with that solitary success coming at Stamford Bridge against Manchester United on October 31.

As per Football Insider, Chelsea are in the market for defensive reinforcements during the upcoming January transfer window, with the Blues conceding 20 goals across their opening 11 Premier League matches.

Departing Stamford Bridge for the Bernabeu on a free transfer in the summer of 2022, Rudiger has fallen down the pecking order at Real Madrid since the arrival of head coach Jose Mourinho.

As a result, it is believed that the 33-year-old veteran could be available for a cut-price fee in the New Year, especially given that his current deal with Los Blancos expires at the end of the season.

Realising that situation, Chelsea are supposedly considering a January swoop for Rudiger, who the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup during a five-year spell in West London.

Failing to feature in any of Real Madrid's past five La Liga contests, the former Germany international is not one of Mourinho's favourites, meaning that a mid-season switch is on the cards.

Focusing in on Stamford Bridge matters for a moment, Chelsea have conceded 12 goals across six Premier League home matches so far, with only bottom side Crystal Palace (13) allowing more on home soil.

Alonso's side are going to struggle massively to pick up regular results on their own patch if they continue to let in an average of two goals per game, relying on their star attackers to bail them out at the other end.

At the age of 33, Rudiger has seen and done it all, and the 86-time international could be a brilliant role model and leader for young defenders Levi Colwill and Josh Acheampong.

Sure it couldn’t happen, could it? Only five times in the history of the Premier League have sides suffered successive relegations from the top tier to the third.

For anyone who witnessed the shambolic showing at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, that nightmare scenario suddenly doesn’t look so  ridiculous. West Ham in the third division, 62,500 seater stadium and all?

Alarming parallels exist between West Ham’s performance this season and that of their former competitors Leicester City who now find themselves playing their football in the third division.

It has been revealed that the Hammers are now in the bottom half of the Championship, with just 24 points from 17 games. At the same stage last season, the Foxes themselves, after 17 games had amassed … Exactly the same number of points.

All of which seemed unimaginable when the Irons beat Swansea five weeks ago to go second, and Nuno Espirito Santo picked upthe September manager of the month award.

According to recent reports, fratton Park showing was a real wake up call to West Ham’s management and board. This ship is sinking.

In a recent development, the only positive is that a month is a long time in this league. A run of form could be just around the corner and any team – West Ham included – can win five or six games and transform their fortunes. But the Hammers’ form at present is most definitely that of a relegation candidate rather than a play-off hopeful.

Which hardly helps the recruitment in January.

For anyone living under the misconception that Leicester City’s case was an isolated example and that lightning couldn’t strike twice, Wolverhampton Wanderers, who were also relegated in 2012/13, had 22 points after 17 games.

According to recent reports, stoke City come calling on Saturday with a seriously impressive run of form, unbeaten in six whereas the Hammers are winless in their last half dozen. No time like the present to get back to winning ways and arrest the downhill slide. One relegation is enough, thank you very much.

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:24.

Aiming to continue an unbeaten streak and break into the top two of the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will welcome Reading to Hillsborough on Saturday.

The hosts sit fourth and two points off second spot after a midweek draw, while their visitors have fallen to ninth spot following three straight defeats.

Sheffield Wednesday head back to Hillsborough on Saturday aiming to continue a positive start to life under Dave Challinor and close in on League One's automatic promotion spots.

He arrived to take over a side winless in four games after a strong start to their first season back in League One and with their sights set on a return to the Championship, as they lost their final two games under Henrik Pedersen and played out two draws under caretaker management.

The Owls were slow off the mark in cup action under the new boss, losing to Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley, but they would win his first two league games at the helm to return to the top six, beating Plymouth Argyle 3-0 and Barnsley 2-1 in an away South Yorkshire Derby thanks to Jamal Lowe's first-half brace.

A tough trip to Stevenage then followed on Tuesday, and the South Yorkshire outfit kept an unbeaten league run under Challinor in tact as the contest ended goalless, meaning they have scored five goals and conceded just one in his first three third-tier games at the helm.

Now sitting fourth and just two points behind third-placed Oxford United and second-placed Huddersfield Town, Sheffield Wednesday will aim to continue their positive run and return to winning ways at Hillsborough with a chance to break into the automatic promotion spots if other results go their way.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip to Yorkshire aiming to bounce back to form and move back within touching distance of the playoff places.

Reading made a positive start to their first full season under Leam Richardson, having also set their sights on challenging for a return to the Championship, earning 21 points from their first 12 games courtesy of six wins and just three defeats.

That culminated in consecutive wins over Leyton Orient and Barnsley, but the Royals have seen their form take a dip since, going on to draw away at Plymouth before suffering three straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Broken up by a 5-0 FA Cup win over Peterborough United, Richardson's men lost 2-0 to Oxford United in League One and in an EFL Trophy penalty shootout to Bristol Rovers, before falling away at league leaders Stockport County and at home to strugglers Bromley last weekend as Victor Adeboyejo scored the only goal on the hour mark to earn Bromley just a third win of the term.

The dip in form has seen Reading drop to ninth spot and four points off the top six, and they will hope to arrest that slump and keep themselves in the top-six picture with a rebound victory in Saturday's tough test.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Reading form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday will likely remain without Reece James, Max Lowe, Tyler Onyango and Mason Burstow on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Di'Shon Bernard and Liam Cooper have returned from injuries and will continue in a back three alongside Sil Swinkels, having kept two clean sheets in the last three games, as long as Cooper is declared fit after another slight concern.

Elsewhere, Jamal Lowe has lined up in a makeshift wing-back role in the absence of James and Lowe, but winger Jordi Liongola took that spot in midweek, while Louie Barry was fit to start at Stevenage after an injury layoff and could continue in support of front man Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Reading duo Paddy Lane and Benn Ward remain confined to the treatment room.

Jack Marriott will continue to lead the line, having netted nine goals in 11 league games this season, although Jamie Reid and Jacob Brown do also have claims for attacking spots, as does Kyreece Lisbie who was suspended last time out alongside Haydon Roberts.

Charlie Savage could also come back in from the outset, after George Earthy and Andy Rinomhota joined Lewis Wing in midfield last time out.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Bannan, J Lowe; Slattery, Keillor-Dunn, Barry.

Reading possible starting lineup:.

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, Knight, O'Connor, Roberts; Wing, Savage; Lisbie, Earthy, Brown; Marriott.

With two wins and a draw in League One since Challinor's appointment, Sheffield Wednesday appear to have rediscovered their groove and have been boosted by returns of several key men in recent weeks.

Taking on a Reading side hit by three straight defeats, we fancy the Owls to bounce back with another clean sheet and victory at Hillsborough at the weekend.

The player overlooked is none other than Pablo Felipe.

Now, before we get ahead of ourselves, I’ve openly never been a big fan of the player. He barely scores any goals, looks slow and has missed some great opportunities in front of goal.

However, while Pablo Felipe may not always grab the headlines, the numbers indicate he is one of the most influential players in our squad.

When Pablo starts, West Ham score first in 83.6% of matches. Without him in the starting line-up, that figure plummets to just 18.2%. In football, scoring first can completely change the course of a game, making this a significant indicator of his influence.

The defensive numbers are equally striking. With Pablo on the pitch, the team have scored 16 goals while conceding only five. Without him, they have scored 19 but conceded 19. While the attacking output remains similar, the defensive stability and overall balance are clearly stronger when he plays.

“Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link? The gaffer could do worse than select Pablo.

This highlights something many supporters already recognise. Pablo’s value lies in his work rate, intelligent positioning, pressing and ability to knit the team together. He helps the side control matches, protects the defence and creates the conditions for others to shine.

With few options and players underperforming, Parker may look to reintegrate the Portuguese striker into the first-team set-up for the visit of Stoke City on Saturday.

The other player who deserves a place in the starting eleven is Tomáš Souček. Despite featuring for just 182 minutes across nine matches, he has already registered three goals and eleven shots. With the team in desperate need of leaders, Souček’s influence could prove invaluable. Fiercely respected within the dressing room, the midfielder has earned the nickname “Iron Man” from his teammates and it’s easy to see why! As Kris has already reported, this hasn’t gone unnoticed elsewhere!

Former manager David Moyes once summed up his importance perfectly: “We rely on him a lot, we need him, and he is very notable for us.”.

According to recent reports, I think we’ve reached a point now where we need some more clarity from West Ham United about the future direction of the football club. Whilst I understand there is an overriding desire to get the Hammers promoted, something which has been described to us by club insiders as a priority, I’m increasingly concerned about how we intend to achieve it.

Because as things stand at the moment, West Ham appear rudderless. In fact, I’d go as far as to say we’re listing. We’re getting progressively worse, and there is a worrying lack of direction at the football club.

Recent findings suggest that whilst there may be a desire to reach a certain destination, I see very little from West Ham at the moment to suggest that we know the route. And that’s why I believe we really need to hear from Daniel Křetínský.

Sources indicate that we’ve waited an awfully long time for the restructuring of West Ham’s shareholding to go through. And whilst Claret & Hugh reported earlier this month that the transactions had been completed, we’re still waiting for public confirmation from the football club.

Křetínský himself has indicated that he will engage with supporters once the share transaction has been finalised, but quite frankly, I don’t think that’s good enough anymore.

West Ham are in desperate need of leadership. Whatever the situation with his shareholding, Křetínský is already in a position of authority at the football club.

West Ham are still waiting for Daniel Kretinsky to address supporters.

Whilst I don’t expect him to be shooting from the lip in the way David Sullivan used to, I do think he needs to provide some leadership, some direction and some communication with supporters as to what the actual plan is here.

Because almost everybody at every level of the football club, from the players right up to the very top, appears to be struggling.

Ideally, I’d like to know what the direction of travel is. What is the strategy for West Ham United?

They want to take us forward, but how are they going to do that? What’s the initiative for January? What’s the plan for investment?

We sold around £200m worth of players during the summer, we’ve yet to see the anticipated injection of funds from the shareholders, and we currently don’t look anything like a team capable of mounting a successful promotion challenge.

And that, by the club’s own admission, is supposed to be the number one priority.

Industry observers note that as things stand, the team are getting worse and the club appear to be getting worse. I don’t think West Ham supporters are being unreasonable in wanting to know what the people running our football club intend to do about it.

We need to hear from Daniel Křetínský.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has mentioned that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

The Liverpool head coach remarked (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

Recent findings suggest that “With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also significant, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

In a recent development, “I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

“I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

Iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

Tottenham Hotspur have eased injury fears regarding Omar Marmoush ahead of Sunday's Premier League trip to Sunderland.

Roberto De Zerbi's troops are up to 10th position in the Premier League table after beating Ipswich Town in North London last weekend, when Luca Williams-Barnett became the third-youngest Premier League scorer in the club's history.

Spurs have a number of fitness concerns ahead of their match at Sunderland on Sunday afternoon, when the Lilywhites will be looking to record a fifth victory in their past six league fixtures.

Following back-to-back 17th-placed finishes in 2025 and 2026, Tottenham are plotting their route back to European qualification, with the Lilywhites supposedly keen on a January move for Inter Milan veteran Hakan Calhanoglu.

However, the Premier League side are said to have suffered a major blow in their pursuit of the well-known Turkey international, who is reportedly wishing to stay put at San Siro in the short-term.

Ahead of the jaunt up to the North-East home of Sunderland on Sunday, Tottenham released an exclusive training video onto their social media channels on Thursday (November 26).

The brief clip demonstrates Marmoush working in the gym alongside his Spurs teammates, allaying fears that the attacker had picked up an injury that would keep him sidelined for the match at the Stadium of Light.

The 27-year-old made a 26-minute cameo for Spurs last time out as they beat Ipswich in North London, and it is understood that the Egyptian made it through that particular appearance unscathed.

However, concerns commenced for Tottenham supporters at the beginning of this week when speculation insisted that the attacker was set for a period on the sidelines after visiting a knee specialist.

Unless De Zerbi's side are pulling the wool over the eyes of supporters and rival clubs, it appears that Marmoush is fully fit and available for an key match at Sunderland this weekend.

Whilst there has been a positive revision on the fitness of Marmoush, Tottenham are prepared to be without the services of both Mathys Tel and Savio for the game at Sunderland on Sunday.

Former Bayern Munich man Tel picked up a hamstring problem during the loss at Leeds United prior to the international break and is expected to be sidelined for up to three weeks.

Savio made his first appearance in over a month during the beating of Ipswich last time out, although the Brazilian was forced off in the closing stages with a recurrence of a muscular matter.

Following the news that Tomáš Souček has the opportunity to leave West Ham for a Premier League club in January, I have to say that I’m becoming extremely worried about the direction of the football club.

Claret & Hugh spoke to one of Souček’s representatives earlier today, and whilst they made it clear that his preference was to help fire West Ham back into the Premier League, it’s clear that he is a man in demand.

One Premier League club in particular is understood to be surprised that Souček has not been playing more frequently for West Ham and, as a result, is happy to test the water to discover whether he’s surplus to requirements at the London Stadium.

In my opinion, this is not something West Ham should consider, not for a moment.

Even before this news, I was going to put forward my case for Souček being involved from the start against Stoke City.

In the absence of any sort of goalscoring form from our strikers, Souček would seem like one of the most likely sources of goals in a team which has gone from being free-scoring and among the top goalscorers in the division to one that struggles to do anything other than hit the woodwork.

It has been revealed that A lot has been made about West Ham having Premier League players, but I’m not sure how many of them truly are. Souček, however, very firmly falls into that category.

He’s a European trophy winner, an international player, a proven Premier League goalscorer and more than capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

This is a player who signed a new West Ham contract only last month and whose commitment to the football club has never really been in question.

But what has just become abundantly clear is that if we don’t use him, we’re likely to lose him.

And I find it highly unlikely that West Ham will be able to bring in a better player than Tomáš Souček in the January transfer window.

Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • In a recent development, city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

In a recent development, city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been revealed.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

It has been revealed that the charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

In a recent development, it would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

However, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is said to be one of the most serious of the 115.

According to recent reports, the damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

It has been revealed that the Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

It has been revealed that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

Sources indicate that city have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

It has been revealed that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for upcoming players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

Industry observers note that on Friday, a City spokesman stated: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and announced in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

City denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

Industry observers note that it did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, remarked: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

In a recent development, “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Recent findings suggest that ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a fresh phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, said he believed the club were innocent.

According to recent reports, “For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder said while on international duty.

“When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

It has been revealed that the Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

As well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

Industry observers note that we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

Industry observers note that city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they noted that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

According to recent reports, at the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also said: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Of the Football Leaks documents, City remarked: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool lost their 100% record in this season’s Champions League with defeat at Fenerbahce three weeks ago, and they’ll be aiming to bounce back tonight with victory away to Club Brugge.

For Reds fans of a certain vintage, the Belgian outfit will evoke happy memories of the triumphant 1976 UEFA Cup final and 1978 European Cup final, with this being the first meeting since the latter success at Wembley.

Andoni Iraola’s satisfaction at Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing of Manchester United has been tempered by ongoing injuries to Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch, with no return date set for the midfielder  as he continues to struggle with a heel problem.

The Liverpool head coach spoke of how he ‘enjoyed analysing’ Club Brugge, who go into this game level on points and goal difference with the Reds and have a red-hot striker in Nicolo Tresoldi, who’s already netted 16 times this season (including a hat-trick against Inter Milan).

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola has made three changes from the starting XI which thumped Man United on Sunday.

Alisson Becker continues between the sticks, and there’s one change to the defence. It’s a surprising one, too, with Virgil van Dijk omitted from the line-up to allow for the reintroduction of Jeremie Frimpong at right-back.

Ronald Araujo duly shuffles across to centre-back to partner Jeremy Jacquet, with Milos Kerkez on the left.

One alteration in midfield sees Trey Nyoni come in for Alexis Mac Allister, with the teenager lining up next to Dominik Szoboszlai.

The third and final change to the starting XI sees Victor Munoz replace Rio Ngumoha in attack, with Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak all keeping their places.
